sample_unit: patients (PET/CT scans, external validation set; 224 for development)

links.outcome: Segmentation DSC improvement and fraction of patients referred when high-uncertainty cases were deferred
links.effect: Referring patients above uncertainty thresholds improved DSC by 4.7% (MC Dropout Ensemble) and 5.0% (Deep Ensemble) while referring 21.8% and 22% of patients.
links.quote: With referring patients based on uncertainty thresholds from 0.85 validation DSC for all uncertainty measures, on average the DSC improved from the full dataset by 4.7% and 5.0% while referring 21.8% and 22% patients for MC Dropout Ensemble and Deep Ensemble, respectively.

unlisted_practices: Uncertainty-based batch and instance referral of auto-segmentations for oropharyngeal cancer radiotherapy planning, comparing uncertainty measures (CV, entropy, mutual information, Dice-risk)

screen.reason: Evaluates uncertainty quantification methods and uncertainty-based referral/deferral thresholds for oropharyngeal cancer radiotherapy segmentation to safeguard performance.
